# Kosmos Minimal Prototype

**Generated by Cursor agent.** Throwaway research code to validate the Kosmos architecture hypothesis: a structured world model coordinates literature and analysis agents across discovery cycles.

## References

- Robin (predecessor): [Nature s41586-026-10652-y](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10652-y)
- Kosmos: [arXiv:2511.02824](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02824)

## Question

Does a structured world model keep literature and analysis agents aligned on one hypothesis thread across cycles, with traceable claims?

This prototype validates **architecture only**, not Kosmos discovery quality at production scale.

## Run

```bash
cd research/kosmos_prototype
uv venv && uv pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py run
python main.py run --no-world-model
```

Artifacts land in `runs/<run_id>/` with per-cycle JSON and `report.md`.

## Success criteria (manual)

1. `kosmos_wm` run: `nucleotide_salvage` hypothesis becomes `supported` with both literature and analysis findings.
2. `report.md` claims link to `evidence_id` values traceable to `cycle_N/*.json`.
3. `--no-world-model` run: cycle 2+ repeats `lit_nucleotide_salvage` and `analysis_group_diff` tasks.

## Layout

- `world_model.py` — structured shared state
- `planner.py` — WM query vs lossy summary ablation
- `agents.py` — deterministic literature/analysis stubs
- `cycle.py` — 3-cycle campaign loop
- `NOTES.md` — validation results, Kosmos gaps, improvement ideas
